title: The full multivariable model, certified: adjusting for age, cognitive speed adds nothing to predicting sway (multiple OLS bit-for-bit vs base R lm, machine precision vs statsmodels)

dataset.name: BDS -- a public data set of human balance evaluations (Santos & Duarte 2016)
dataset.record: per subject: eyes-closed-foam COP path length (response), Trail Making Test A time and age (predictors); n=158
dataset.citation: Santos DA, Duarte M. A public data set of human balance evaluations. PeerJ 2016;4:e2648. doi:10.7717/peerj.2648.

proposition: The partial-correlation sibling showed the sway-cognition association is largely age-confounded; its open question called for a fuller multivariable model. The NEWLY-AUTHORED multipleRegression fits sway ~ age + Trail Making Test A, reproducing base R stats::lm bit-for-bit and statsmodels OLS to machine precision. In the joint model age is the dominant, highly significant predictor (beta 1.59 cm/year, p=2e-8) while TMT-A's independent contribution is not significant (beta 0.12, p=0.55); the model explains ~28% of sway variance (R-squared 0.276, F(2,155)=29.5, p=1.4e-11). Cognitive processing speed adds essentially nothing beyond age.

validation.reference: The newly-authored multipleRegression op (multivariable OLS via the same QR decomposition as base R) is validated against BOTH base R stats::lm/summary.lm AND statsmodels OLS on the identical response and predictors -- a double reference. The coefficients match base R lm BIT-FOR-BIT (|diff| = 0; standard errors, p-values, R-squared and F to ~1e-14) and statsmodels OLS to machine precision (coef |diff| ~1e-13). The eyes-closed-foam sway comes from PhysioMoCap::swayMetrics (path_length, certified against Prieto in the sibling sway-posturography-bds case).
validation.data: REAL -- Santos & Duarte (2016) BDS; eyes-closed-foam COP path length on age and TMT-A, n=158
validation.note: The reproducible findings are (1) multipleRegression reproduces base R lm bit-for-bit and statsmodels OLS to machine precision; (2) cognitive speed adds nothing to predicting sway beyond age. HONEST scope: (1) this AUTHORS A NEW OP, multipleRegression (multivariable OLS via the same QR decomposition as base R; response in the first column, predictors in the rest), the many-predictor generalisation of linearRegression, and reuses the certified swayMetrics-derived sway; (2) the coefficients reproduce base R stats::lm BIT-FOR-BIT (|diff| = 0; SE, p, R-squared and F to ~1e-14) and statsmodels OLS to MACHINE PRECISION (coef |diff| ~1e-13); (3) the finding: in the joint model AGE is the dominant, highly significant predictor (beta = 1.59 cm per year, p = 2e-8) while TMT-A's independent contribution is NOT significant (beta = 0.12, p = 0.55) once age is controlled; the model explains about 28% of the between-subject variance in sway (R-squared = 0.276, adjusted 0.267, F(2,155) = 29.5, p = 1.4e-11); so cognitive processing speed adds essentially nothing to predicting sway beyond age -- the complete multivariable picture behind the partial correlation; the TMT p-value here equals the partial-correlation p exactly (the coefficient t-test IS the partial-correlation test); (4) a cross-sectional cohort (ASSOCIATION, NOT causation); a linear additive model without an interaction term; run_simulation = FALSE (deterministic).

open_questions.q: The model is linear and additive; an age x cognition interaction, non-linear age terms, or additional predictors (vestibular, strength, medication) might reveal structure this two-predictor model cannot. The complete two-predictor OLS shown here is the honest resolution of the partial-correlation case's call for a fuller model. Documented, not escalated.
